image_description: A vintage black typewriter viewed from a high angle. The image focuses on the keyboard area, specifically highlighting the long, white space bar at the bottom center of the key layout. The keys are circular with white tops and black bodies. The carriage and platen are visible at the top.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The space bar is significantly longer than the circular type keys, visually appearing to be about 8-10 times the diameter of a single key.

artifact_observations.location: Platen roller and ribbon cover area
artifact_observations.reasoning: The black fabric/ribbon area behind the keys exhibits a smeared, painterly texture rather than distinct mechanical details or fabric weave. It looks like AI-generated noise or melting.

The metallic structure on the right side connecting the carriage to the base lacks clear geometric definition. It appears to blend into the background with soft, undefined edges, suggesting structural ambiguity.

The alignment of the circular keys is slightly irregular. Some rows curve unnaturally, and the spacing between keys varies inconsistently, deviating from the rigid grid expected in mechanical devices.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific identification of the object as a space bar within the context of a typewriter, distinguishing it from other elongated keys.
To verify the 3D structural integrity of the mechanical parts, especially the ambiguous right-side hinge and the depth relationship between keys and the platen.
To check for edge bleeding or fusion between the white space bar and the black keyboard chassis, ensuring clean boundaries.

focus_areas: Boundary sharpness between white keys and black body
Structural logic of the carriage assembly
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'smearing' effect in the dark mechanical areas (ribbon/platen). This is a common AI artifact where complex mechanical details fail to resolve. Also, verify if the space bar's length is physically proportional to the rest of the keyboard layout, as AI often misjudges scale in repetitive structures.
